title: It Isn't a Quite Dead Garden
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from The Secret Garden by Frances Hodgson Burnett (1911).
body: She did not skip, but walked. She went slowly and kept her eyes on the ground. She looked in the old border beds and among the grass, and after she had gone round, trying to miss nothing, she had found ever so many more sharp, pale green points, and she had become quite excited again.
“It isn’t a quite dead garden,” she cried out softly to herself. “Even if the roses are dead, there are other things alive.”

She did not know anything about gardening, but the grass seemed so thick in some of the places where the green points were pushing their way through that she thought they did not seem to have room enough to grow. She searched about until she found a rather sharp piece of wood and knelt down and dug and weeded out the weeds and grass until she made nice little clear places around them.

“Now they look as if they could breathe,” she said, after she had finished with the first ones. “I am going to do ever so many more. I’ll do all I can see. If I haven’t time today I can come tomorrow.”

She went from place to place, and dug and weeded, and enjoyed herself so immensely that she was led on from bed to bed and into the grass under the trees. The exercise made her so warm that she first threw her coat off, and then her hat, and without knowing it she was smiling down on to the grass and the pale green points all the time.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did Mary find as she looked in the old border beds?
options: Sharp, pale green points
Bright red roses
Fallen autumn leaves
A hidden garden key

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what did Mary use to dig and weed?
options: A rather sharp piece of wood
A small garden trowel
Her bare hands only
A pair of scissors

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did Mary do with the weeds and grass around the green points?
options: Dug and weeded them out to make clear places
Left them alone so as not to disturb the soil
Covered them with more soil
Pulled up the green points along with them

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what two things did Mary throw off because the exercise made her warm?
options: Her coat and her hat
Her shoes and her gloves
Her scarf and her shawl
Her apron and her bonnet

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did Mary say about the roses in the garden?
options: Even if the roses are dead, there are other things alive
The roses were the only living thing left
The roses had already begun to bloom again
She did not care whether the roses were alive

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why did Mary clear grass away from the green points?
options: She thought they didn't have room enough to grow
She wanted to plant new seeds there
She thought the grass was diseased
She was told to by a gardener

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does Mary mean when she says the cleared plants "look as if they could breathe"?
options: Clearing space around them let them grow more freely
The plants had literally started breathing air
The plants looked like they were wilting
The plants had grown taller overnight

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, how did Mary feel about her work in the garden?
options: She was excited and thoroughly enjoyed herself
She found the work tedious and dull
She felt guilty for disturbing the garden
She was anxious about being caught

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the overall point of the passage?
options: Mary discovered signs of life in the garden and eagerly began clearing space for them to grow
Mary decided the garden was completely dead and gave up on it
Mary planted an entirely new garden from seeds she had brought
Mary was told by someone else exactly what to plant

questions.prompt: As used in the passage, what does it mean that Mary went about "trying to miss nothing"?
options: Trying to overlook or skip nothing
Trying to walk as quietly as possible
Trying to avoid stepping on the grass
Trying to finish as quickly as possible

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what did Mary decide to do if she didn't have time to finish that day?
options: Come back tomorrow
Ask a gardener to finish for her
Leave the garden as it was
Work through the night

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where did Mary's search eventually lead her?
options: From bed to bed and into the grass under the trees
Out through the garden gate and down the road
Back into the house to fetch tools
Toward a locked door covered in ivy

questions.prompt: Per the passage, how did Mary walk as she searched the garden?
options: Slowly, keeping her eyes on the ground
Quickly, glancing all around her
Backward, so as not to miss anything behind her
On tiptoe, trying not to make noise

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did Mary say softly to herself?
options: It isn't a quite dead garden
I wish I had never come here
Someone must have planted these
I am too tired to continue

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why was Mary unaware that she had thrown off her coat and hat?
options: She was so absorbed in her digging and weeding that she didn't notice
She had planned in advance to remove them
Someone else removed them for her
The weather had suddenly turned very cold

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes how Mary spent her time in this passage?
options: She searched the garden bed by bed, clearing space around every green shoot she found
She sat and admired the garden without touching anything
She waited for a gardener to show her what to do
She spent her time picking flowers to bring inside

questions.prompt: As used in the passage, what does it mean that Mary had become quite "excited" again?
options: Filled with eager, lively feeling
Very tired and ready to rest
Confused about what to do next
Annoyed at how much work remained
